question: ap1
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Hysteresis loops, borrowed from ferromagnetism
ideas.description: Slowly ramp a stimulus (e.g., TPA, EGF, or drug dose) up and then back down. At each step, measure single-cell AP-1 activity with a live reporter, plus AP-1 motif accessibility with scATAC. If the downward path does not retrace the upward path (an open hysteresis loop, with a width that persists over time), the system has memory; if AP-1 motifs are knocked out, that memory should disappear.

ideas.title: Write vs. refresh test, modeled on DRAM
ideas.description: In computer DRAM, stored data fades unless it is periodically refreshed. By analogy, use an inducible degron (dTAG-FOS/JUN or a dominant-negative A-FOS) to remove AP-1 at different times after a transient stimulus. Then measure whether chromatin accessibility and the faster re-response persist. This tells you whether AP-1 only writes the memory (it survives removal) or must keep refreshing it (it decays with a measurable time constant).

ideas.title: Twin-study heritability with lineage barcodes
ideas.description: Borrowing heritability estimation from quantitative genetics, use lineage barcoding (e.g., Rewind or ClonMapper) to track sister and cousin cells across several divisions after a stimulus. Then calculate how strongly AP-1 target accessibility and expression correlate within each lineage. If the correlation within clones decays slowly across generations, and does so more slowly than for non-AP-1 programs, that is evidence AP-1 carries a state that cells inherit.

ideas.title: Measuring the system's response to pulses, as in signal processing
ideas.description: Use optogenetic ERK/RAS control or microfluidics to deliver pulse trains that vary in frequency, duration, and spacing. Then fit linear and nonlinear transfer-function models to AP-1 reporter dynamics and downstream enhancer opening. If the fitted decay time constant is much longer than the turnover of AP-1 protein and mRNA, the memory sits downstream of AP-1 (e.g., in chromatin), not in AP-1 levels themselves.

ideas.title: Prime-boost recall test with edited AP-1 motifs, borrowed from vaccination
ideas.description: Prime cells, let them rest until AP-1 levels return to baseline, then challenge them again and measure how fast and how strongly AP-1 target genes respond, including in contexts such as drug-resistance priming. Repeat this in lines where base editing has destroyed the AP-1 motifs at specific memory enhancers. Losing the faster, stronger second response without changing the first response would show that the memory is carried at those AP-1 sites.
